title: Zuccotto
subtitle: The Florentine dome dessert: sponge-lined bowl filled with ricotta, chocolate, and toasted nuts
excerpt: Zuccotto is an Italian dome-shaped dessert assembled upside down in a bowl: sponge slices line the bowl, a ricotta and chocolate filling goes in, and when the bowl is unmoulded the dome sits on its flat base. The flavours are simple, the method is straightforward, and the result is impressive at the table.
sourceNotes: Zuccotto (from the Italian zucca, meaning pumpkin or skull, for the dome shape) is associated with Florence and the Medici court. A standard form of the recipe using ricotta, dark chocolate, toasted nuts, and a liqueur-soaked sponge has been documented consistently in Italian patisserie literature since the twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Zuccotto freezes very well. Cover with cling film and freeze the whole dome for up to 1 month. Serve semi-frozen for a different texture, or thaw in the fridge for 3 hours.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Must be made at least 6 hours ahead and keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. The sponge absorbs the brandy and softens further as it sits.

glossaryTerms.definition: The technique of lining a round bowl with food-wrap, then with sponge slices that overlap slightly, filling the cavity with a set mixture, sealing with more sponge, chilling until firm, and inverting the bowl onto a plate to reveal the dome shape. The flat base of the sponge becomes the top when unmoulded.

content.text: Zuccotto is built upside down. The

method means there is no baking involved in the finished dessert; only the sponge lining needs to be made or bought. Use a bought plain sponge, madeira cake, or savoiardi if you prefer not to bake the sponge from scratch.
You will also need about 300 g of plain sponge, madeira cake, or savoiardi to line the bowl.

Line a 1.2 to 1.5 litre pudding basin or round mixing bowl with two layers of cling film, leaving plenty of overhang. Cut the sponge into slices about 1 cm thick and use them to line the bowl completely, overlapping the slices slightly so there are no gaps. Press firmly against the sides.
Mix the brandy with 2 tablespoons of water and brush the sponge lining generously to moisten it.
Beat the ricotta with the icing sugar and vanilla until smooth and creamy. Fold in the whipped cream. Add the chopped dark chocolate and hazelnuts and fold through.
Spoon the filling into the lined bowl and smooth the top. Cover with the remaining sponge slices to seal the filling in. Fold the cling film over the top. Chill for at least 6 hours.

Place a flat plate over the bowl and invert. Lift the bowl away and peel off the cling film. Dust the dome generously with cocoa powder or icing sugar through a fine sieve. Serve in slices like a cake, cut from the top of the dome downward.
